system_prompt_style.evidence_quote: In the prompts, we set some injectable slots such as {{ Demonstrations }} and {{ Candidate Models }}. These slots are uniformly replaced with the corresponding text before being fed into the LLM.
system_prompt_style.note: Paper only; stage-specific prompts with slots (task list, demos, chat logs, candidate models).

env_context_strategy.evidence_quote: we first filter out models based on their task type to select the ones that match the current task. Among these selected models, we rank them based on the number of downloads
env_context_strategy.note: Closest value: candidate model descriptions are selected by task-type filter and download ranking (not lexical retrieval) and injected into the prompt. Ambiguity: environment context is a model catalogue, not a repository.

context_compaction.note: Paper only; no config or code available. Top-K model filtering reduces prompt tokens but is not history compaction.

observation_format.evidence_quote: These inference results are presented in a structured format, such as bounding boxes with detection probabilities in the object detection model, answer distributions in the question-answering model, etc.
observation_format.note: Paper only. Media outputs are referenced by file path, not passed as images.

tool_call_format.evidence_quote: generating a list of tasks with the following format: [{"task": task, "id", task_id, "dep": dependency_task_ids, "args":

tool_count.note: Tools are HF models selected dynamically; task list is not enumerated in the evidence.

edit_primitive.evidence_quote: The task must be selected from the following options: {{ Available Task List }}.
edit_primitive.note: Actions are AI-model tasks; no file-editing primitive is described. Coded from the task registry slot in the prompt. This is only a paper-level reading.

tool_schema_source.evidence_quote: {"model_id": model id #1, "metadata": meta-info #1, "description": description of model #1}
tool_schema_source.note: Model descriptions are taken from Hugging Face model cards (community-authored).

protocol_standardization.note: No code/dependencies in evidence to grep.

loop_primitives.evidence_quote: Its workflow includes four stages: task planning, model selection, task execution, and response generation

planning_granularity.evidence_quote: LLM parses the user request into a task list and determines the execution order and resource dependencies among tasks
planning_granularity.note: JSON task DAG with dep fields.

multi_agent_topology.evidence_quote: With an LLM (e.g., ChatGPT) as the core controller and the expert models as the executors
multi_agent_topology.note: Expert models are tools, not agents.

delegation_mechanism.evidence_quote: With an LLM (e.g., ChatGPT) as the core controller and the expert models as the executors
delegation_mechanism.note: Expert models are non-agentic tools, not delegated agents.

short_term_state.evidence_quote: HuggingGPT dynamically replaces this symbol with the resource generated by the prerequisite task
short_term_state.note: Task list plus resource map held across stages.

self_verification.note: The GPT-4 critic is used only for evaluation, not in the harness.

termination_condition.note: The pipeline ends after response generation; no condition mechanism is described.

execution_isolation.evidence_quote: Expert models on hybrid endpoints execute the assigned tasks
execution_isolation.note: Hybrid HF inference endpoints plus local endpoints.

eval_hooks.note: The paper reports evaluations, but no repo is available to check for a shipped runner.

target_domain.evidence_quote: HuggingGPT is able to tackle generalized AI tasks covering multiple modalities and domains
target_domain.note: Multimodal AI-model orchestration. The closest value is general_tool_use.

open_source.note: The repo URL is given (https://github.com/microsoft/JARVIS), but no LICENSE is in the evidence.

model_agnostic.evidence_quote: we employed the gpt-3.5-turbo, text-davinci-003 and gpt-4 variants of the GPT models as the main LLMs
model_agnostic.note: The paper also evaluates Alpaca and Vicuna as controllers. No client abstraction is visible.

primary_artifact.note: Only the paper was available; the repo was not pinned.

first_release_date.note: Only the v4 date is visible (2023-12-03); v1 date and repo tags are not in the evidence.

pinned_version.note: No tag or commit in the evidence.
